turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the system's crawling, I'm still on the log-in screen. What have you come about?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the burning again when I wee. I know I go on, but it's this hot stinging right at the end, and I've been up and down to the loo like nobody's business.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): The screen just flicked back to someone else's notes. Burning when you pass urine? Say that once more.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, burning every time I wee. It started Saturday night, so that's four days, and I feel I haven't emptied properly afterwards.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Four days. Are you going more often as well?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Constantly. Every half hour, even at night, and only a trickle comes out, then I'm desperate again two minutes later. It's wearing me out.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the urine?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood. I checked because last time there was a pink tinge, but this time it's ordinary colour, maybe a shade darker if I haven't drunk, but not blood.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. First time, or has this happened before?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): This is the third time this year... well, actually, maybe the fourth. There was March, when I didn't bother coming in, then June, September, and now. So maybe the fourth.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fourth this year, roughly. Sorry, the template's jumped. Any fever, or pain over the kidneys in your back?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No temperature. I used the thermometer yesterday and it was normal, no shivering, and my back's fine, no loin pain. I was scared it had gone up to the kidneys but it hasn't.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any nausea or vomiting?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, my stomach's been fine. I'm eating normally, no sickness at all. I even had toast this morning, which I mention only because I usually can't face breakfast if I'm properly ill.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): And, the box on here wants me to ask, any vaginal discharge or itching?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. It's purely the wee. I'd rather not go into all that, if you don't mind, it's embarrassing.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): We can park that. What have you taken for it?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): This is the embarrassing bit. My sister had leftover yellow capsules for a water infection and I borrowed them. I know you're not meant to.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hold on, reception's buzzing me about a script. Yellow capsules from your sister, did you say? Which antibiotic?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I thought the box said amoxicillin. No, I looked again this morning, it definitely said trimethoprim. Little yellow water-infection capsules. Two hundred milligrams... no, the strip says one hundred.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the dose got lost, I was clicking the wrong tab. Say the dose and how you took them once more.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): One hundred milligrams, one twice a day, for two days. Four capsules, finished yesterday morning, and none since.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped yesterday morning. Any better for them?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): A tiny bit yesterday afternoon, then this morning the burning is just as bad, worse if I hold on.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. I'm just finding the microbiology form. Keep going.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I also drank pints of cranberry juice, the expensive stuff from the supermarket, and it did nothing. I don't know why I bother, the bottle's still in the car.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cranberry won't clear an infection on its own. Any other regular medicines? The list on screen is blank and I don't trust it.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Only a vitamin D from the chemist, one a day. Nothing else, no blood pressure tablets. I'm thirty-eight, by the way. The notes said forty-one last time and that was wrong.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thirty-eight, I'll fix that later if it lets me. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing I know of. Penicillin was fine when I had it as a child for tonsils, no rash or anything.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Do you smoke, and any chance you could be pregnant? Both boxes are flashing at me.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoked. I can't be pregnant, the coil's in, and my period was two weeks ago, completely normal. I live with my partner, nothing complicated there.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pop on the couch and I'll feel your tummy. Abdomen's soft, no tenderness low down, and your loins aren't sore when I tap them.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): When you press low down in the middle that's a bit uncomfortable, not agony, more a bruised feeling.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, sorry, I said no tenderness and I was half reading the screen. There is a little tenderness just above the pubic bone.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the spot, yes. Low down in the middle.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Earlier you were sure there was no vaginal irritation. Is that still right?

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, I wasn't completely straight with you. There's a bit of soreness on the outside, and a small amount of creamy discharge. It's been a couple of days, and it's worse when I wipe.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Any smell to it, or pain with sex?

[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No smell really. We haven't been intimate since this started, so I can't tell you about that. I just didn't want to say the discharge bit out loud, which is silly at my age.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything that eases the soreness?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): A warm bath helps for a little while, then it comes straight back. I had one last night and nearly fell asleep in it, the day had been that long.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm going to send urine off to the lab. Mid-stream sample, culture, especially as you've already had the trimethoprim.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I do that here? I can go, I've been holding, which I always do in waiting rooms when I'm nervous. The magazines in there are from about 2014, I noticed.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, before you leave. We'll dip it here as well. I'm ordering both the dip and the culture.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): And antibiotics today? Work is a nightmare, I do reception at the dental practice and the loo is down two corridors.

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd rather not start another antibiotic until we see what grows. Two days of trimethoprim already may have muddied the sample. Fever or pain in the back would change that.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): So nothing to take? Not even those cystitis sachets from Boots?

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): You can buy a simple cystitis sachet from the chemist if you want, for the stinging. I'm not prescribing an antibiotic. Drink plenty of water, and please don't take anyone else's leftover tablets again.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I won't. That was daft. My sister will be furious I mentioned her. She had the same thing in the summer, that's why the capsules were in her cupboard.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): You don't catch these off family, usually. Any diabetes in the family, or have you been told you have it? It's prompting me.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): My dad's got type two diabetes. I've never been told I have it, though I haven't had a blood test in ages, so I can't swear to the numbers.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Father with type two, noted. No blood test today. This is most likely another lower urine infection, cystitis, but I want the culture before I'm sure.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): And the discharge? I keep thinking thrush, because of the antibiotic, but I don't actually know. I google too much, that's my problem.

[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): It could be irritation from the urine infection, or early thrush after the antibiotic. I can't separate those today, so that's a possibility beside the cystitis, not a definite diagnosis.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. What if the burning just carries on?
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it's not settling in three days, or sooner if you get a fever or pain in your back, come back and we'll see you. The lab rings through if something needs acting on.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Three days. And the usual things, drinking, front to back?
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Plenty of fluids, wipe front to back, and try not to hold on. That's the advice I'd go with.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll do the sample now. Sorry for rambling, I do it when I'm nervous, and the parking meter's probably run out, which is a saga for another day.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're alright. Pot's on the side. Hand it to reception when you're done and we'll take it from there.

spec.situation: Woman with burning urine again; says 'third time this year' then corrects to 'maybe the fourth'; took leftover antibiotic from a sister; embarrassed; vaginal symptoms denied, then partly admitted. Urine test ordered.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Sister's water infection is mentioned, but not as family history of the patient.
Patient later reports external soreness and discharge; prior denial no longer stands.

omissions.text: Current episode started Saturday night, four days before review.
Urinary frequency is every half hour including at night, causing fatigue/'wearing me out'.
No temperature was measured at home yesterday with a normal thermometer reading.

No vaginal discharge was initially denied, but later the patient corrected this and reported a small amount of creamy discharge and external soreness; the earlier negative finding for vaginal discharge is therefore incorrect.
Trimethoprim course details include four capsules total, finished yesterday morning, with none since.
Only regular medication is over-the-counter vitamin D once daily; specifically denies any blood pressure tablets.
Patient states she is 38 years old and that a previous note saying 41 was wrong.
No known drug allergies, with specific tolerance of penicillin in childhood and no rash.
Pregnancy denial supported by coil in situ and a normal period two weeks ago.

On abdominal examination there was discomfort/tenderness low down in the middle when pressed, described by the patient as 'a bruised feeling, not agony'; the doctor corrected an initial mistaken statement of no tenderness.
No pain with sex could be assessed because she and her partner had not been intimate since symptoms started.
Warm bath gives temporary relief of the external soreness.
Doctor explicitly decided not to prescribe/start another antibiotic today until urine culture result, because 2 days of trimethoprim may have muddied the sample.
Doctor said fever or back pain would change the decision about starting antibiotics.
Doctor noted no blood test today.

There is diagnostic uncertainty/disagreement resolved in the consultation: doctor says this is most likely lower UTI/cystitis but wants culture before being sure; discharge/soreness could be irritation from UTI or early thrush after antibiotic and is not a definite diagnosis.

Family history was recorded wrongly: the sister having a 'water infection' was not family history relevant to the patient; it was mentioned only to explain the source of the leftover trimethoprim capsules.
